t: For necessary expenses in carrying out fossil energy research and development activities, under the authority of the Department of Energy Organization Act (Public Law 95–91), $711,435,000, to remain available until expended: Provided, That no part of the sum herein appropriated shall be used for the field testing of nuclear explosives in the recovery of oil and gas.

fable.w: This is a pure appropriation for fossil energy research and development with a restriction on using funds for field testing nuclear explosives. No tempting reading really exists: it contains no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government.
fable.s: For necessary expenses in carrying out fossil energy research and development activities, under the authority of the Department of Energy Organization Act (Public Law 95–91), $711,435,000, to remain available until expended

qwen_block.w: This section is a standard appropriations provision that allocates funds for specific activities and places a restriction on their use. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or participation with entities outside the federal government. The text involves only the allocation of federal resources and internal restrictions on their expenditure.
qwen_block.s: For necessary expenses in carrying out fossil energy research and development activities, under the authority of the Department of Energy Organization Act (Public Law 95–91), $711,435,000, to remain available until expended: Provided, That no part of the sum herein appropriated shall be used for the field testing of nuclear explosives in the recovery of oil and gas.

opus.w: This is a plain appropriation for fossil energy research and development, with a proviso barring the money from being used for field testing of nuclear explosives. It names no outside party and creates no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue. The reference to the Department of Energy Organization Act only cites where the authority comes from and does not create any participation process.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The "Department of Energy Organization Act" might seem like a source of procedural duties. But this section only sets an appropriation amount and a limit on how the money can be used. No one outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing, or allowed to comment. No rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue is created.

qwen_chat.w: This section is an appropriation provision that authorizes funding for research and development activities and places a restriction on the use of those funds (prohibiting field testing of nuclear explosives). It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government. The actors involved are the federal government (Department of Energy) and the funding source (Congress), both of which are inside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: For necessary expenses in carrying out fossil energy research and development activities, under the authority of the Department of Energy Organization Act (Public Law 95–91), $711,435,000, to remain available until expended: Provided, That no part of the sum herein appropriated shall be used for the field testing of nuclear explosives in the recovery of oil and gas.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "carrying out... activities" implies some form of engagement with external parties, but the text is purely an appropriation clause with a restriction on use of funds. It does not mandate any specific process of consultation, hearing, or coordination with non-federal entities. The restriction on nuclear explosives is a prohibition, not a participation mechanism.
